summary.text: James Walkinshaw is the Democratic incumbent seeking his first full term representing Virginia's 11th District, having won a 2025 special election after Rep. Gerry Connolly's death. He worked for more than a decade as Connolly's chief of staff and served on the Fairfax County Board of Supervisors from 2020 to 2025. In the House he serves on the Oversight and Government Reform and Homeland Security committees and, according to his official biography, focuses on the federal workforce and government operations.

paragraphs.text: Walkinshaw was born on October 22, 1982, in Arlington, Virginia, and grew up in Prince William County.
He graduated from New York University in 2005 with a B.A. in politics.

He then worked in Congress for more than a decade as chief of staff to Rep. Gerry Connolly, advising on federal policy, constituent services and regional priorities such as Metro funding and federal workforce protections, and he had earlier managed Connolly's 2007 and 2008 campaigns.
Walkinshaw served on the Fairfax County Board of Supervisors, representing the Braddock District, from 2020 to September 2025, and chaired the board's Legislative and Environmental committees.

He represented Fairfax County on the Metropolitan Washington Council of Governments, chaired the Regional Transportation Planning Board, and chaired the Virginia Railway Express Operations Board in 2023.

After Connolly's death in May 2025, he won a 10-candidate Democratic primary in June 2025 with about 60% of the vote and then the September 9, 2025 special election over Republican Stewart Whitson, and he was sworn in the next day.
In the House, Walkinshaw serves on the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, including its Military and Foreign Affairs Subcommittee, and the Committee on Homeland Security.

He founded and co-chairs the Federal Workforce Caucus with Rep. Steny Hoyer and Sen. Chris Van Hollen, and he is also a member of the New Democrat Coalition, the Sustainable Energy and Environment Coalition and the Congressional Asian Pacific American Caucus.

The district includes most of Fairfax County, the City of Fairfax, and the towns of Vienna and Herndon. According to his official biography, Walkinshaw lives in Fairfax with his wife, Yvette, and their son, Mateo.
